Hi Evelyn and Karthik,

Attached are the updated quote (OEM_Quote_v2.pdf) and an initial lead-time schedule (leadtime_schedule.xlsx) for the Dedicated 8xA100 tranche we discussed for Brio Labs. Key callouts: 

- Minimum order quantity and tranche cadence are noted on page 2 of the quote.
- Current ETA for full fulfillment is ~18-22 weeks from PO acceptance; we can do a partial first shipment (25% of units) at ~10-12 weeks to meet your Q4 onramp window if Brio confirms commitment to the full tranche.
- Pricing in the quote reflects a staged discount if the customer signs for the full reserved capacity within 30 days.

We flagged cloud backfill as an option — see tab ‘Cloud Bridge’ in the schedule. If you want us to coordinate directly with the cloud partner for an interim capacity hold, tell us which contact to loop in and we’ll send a bridging confirmation.

Subject: Re: Preliminary quote + phased lead times for Brio Labs (BRIO-2028-0042)

Elena —

Thanks for the swift turnaround and for surfacing the partial-shipment option. A few clarifying asks so we can map to the customer's go-live: 

1) For the 25% partial shipment, do you need a separate PO or will the PO reference a phased delivery schedule under a single contract? The procurement team at Brio prefers a single PO with milestone delivery dates.

2) On the Cloud Bridge tab: what is the mechanism you expect the cloud partner to implement? Is it reserved instances on a marketplace listing (short-term) or a capacity hold that counts against their internal quotas? Any wording we can share with Brio procurement to make the fallback concrete will help.

3) Can you confirm customs/shipping buffers for EMEA vs US deltas — Brio has a small EU region they may want capacity for later in the roadmap.

Looping Ben to confirm our side’s preferred procurement language and Marissa to keep product aware of any SKU splits.

Next step: if you can provide a one-page exec summary of the phased fulfillment approach we can include with the customer packet.

—Evelyn

From: Elena Morales <elena@oemsolutions.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jul 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preliminary quote + phased lead times for Brio Labs (BRIO-2028-0042)

Evelyn —

Answers inline: 

1) PO cadence: We can accept a single PO that references the phased delivery schedule (preferred). We’ll mark shipment milestones in the contract and produce pro forma invoices for each tranche. That keeps Brio’s procurement process simple.

2) Cloud Bridge mechanics: We typically offer two options with our channel cloud partners: 
  - Marketplace reserved blocks: partner publishes a temporary reserved block that Redwood (or Brio) can acquire quickly for interim needs. This is the fastest route (days) but is priced as a short-term reserved SKU.
  - Capacity hold: partner commits a quota slot tied to a partner agreement; that is non-billable until consumed but requires the partner (cloud vendor) to confirm quota internally (takes longer, requires PO and partner-to-partner agreement).

I recommend the marketplace reserved block for Brio’s Q4 needs and then swap to OEM hardware when the tranche ships. I’ve copied the cloud contact we use for the reserved block conversations if you want them to confirm availability.

3) Customs/shipping: US shipments are typically 10–14 business days from factory departure; EU routes add ~7–10 business days depending on port congestion — we’ve accounted for that in the leadtime_schedule.xlsx.

I’ll draft a one-page staged-fulfillment summary and send within EOD.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Enterprise Sales, OEM Solutions
elena@oemsolutions.com

Subject: Re: Cloud Bridge: reserved blocks & bridge terms for Brio Labs

Hi all — Samir on the cloud partnerships team. Elena, thanks for the heads up. We can provision a marketplace reserved block for the 25% interim capacity and have a short-term SKU that Redwood can claim on behalf of Brio. Notes: 

- Marketplace listing: https://marketplace.cloudvendor.com/listings/redwood-bridge-reserved (public listing, limited inventory).
- Short-term reserved pricing is about 12% premium to standard committed reserved pricing; we can discount if the OEM confirms full-tranche intent on record.
- We can also do a partner quota hold if Redwood needs guaranteed non-market exposure; that requires a partner-to-partner SOW and ~10 business days to put into effect.

If you want, I can open a marketplace hold for 30 days while legal/PO is worked; I just need the customer name and an internal reference (deal id).

1) Brio to sign single PO referencing phased delivery schedule (Evelyn to drive).
2) OEM (Elena) to deliver one-page staged-fulfillment summary and confirm pro-forma invoice process (due: 2028-07-07 COB).
3) Cloud (Samir) to place a 30-day marketplace hold against the reserved block for Brio (deal id BRIO-2028-0042) and confirm pricing (due: 2028-07-08 17:00 PT).
4) Redwood (Ben/Karthik) to prepare procurement language for the single-PO conditioned on tranche milestone acceptance and customs liability clauses (first draft due: 2028-07-09).

Can everyone confirm by EOD tomorrow on the due dates above? Once confirmed, I’ll attach the MAP to the customer packet and share with Brio procurement.

Attachments for internal packet: cloud_bridge_terms.pdf (summary of marketplace hold vs partner quota).
